problem: A design in design mode never states how the system will be structured at runtime. The design directory carries three diagrams keyed to the narrative levels: a container overview, a sequence flow, and a class inventory of data types. Nothing in the set answers Nexus's question of which services, libraries, data stores, and external systems the design will create and which protocol crosses each boundary. Nothing validates the drafted architecture before the engineer reads it, so the engineer is the only pair of independent eyes on a draft the drafting session wrote. And when a design introduces an endpoint surface or an entity model, those contracts exist only in prose inside the ADR or the class diagram, nowhere reviewable as a whole.
why_now: The comparison against Nexus's pipeline workflow landed this week and showed both systems arriving at the same generate-review-approve shape with different enforcement. Nexus's architecture brief specifies the runtime diagram contract and the pass-cube evaluation gate; harnesses and models now follow skill instructions well enough that a session-spawned reviewer and a named diagram contract need no new install surface. The RED/GREEN/VALIDATE roles already prove the independent-reviewer pattern works in this family, and the viewer record index gives every new artifact a place to land without new joins.
approach: One named diagram slot, one optional artifact, one stage-6 reviewer. The runtime architecture diagram lives at docs/architecture/designs/<name>/diagrams/runtime-architecture.mmd, compiled by build_index.py to record["diagrams"]["runtime"] and rendered by the viewer as the lead tile inside the design's architecture level, ahead of the class diagram, with the level-1 overview untouched as the leading diagram of the design. Its contract is a new shared reference, shared/skills/mermaid/references/architecture-diagram.md, translating Nexus's hard rules: clustered boundaries for client, api, data, infra, and external; shape semantics for services, data stores, libraries, and external systems; every boundary edge labeled with its protocol; 8 to 30 nodes; one page. Stage 6 spawns a reviewer before the engineer reads: it validates the draft against a blind rubric derived from goal.json and intent.json, then re-explores alternatives seeded with the final draft, and its findings enter stage 6 as classified challenges the engineer adjudicates. contracts.md joins the design directory as an optional artifact carrying the envisioned API endpoints and data models, shown before write, skipped with a stated reason when the design touches no public interface. Reviewer spawns run on glm-5.3-flash:cloud per the engineer's standing directive.

alternatives.option: Reserve diagrams/level-0.mmd and shift the numbered levels so the runtime diagram leads the design
alternatives.rejected_because: The numbered keys are load-bearing everywhere: build_index.py compiles by the level-{1,2,3} filename loop, the viewer's record tiles filter the levels list, and the readiness check fails a level whose key is empty. Renumbering risks every consumer at once, and the engineer asked that the overview keep leading the design.

alternatives.option: Make the runtime diagram the design's fourth narrative level
alternatives.rejected_because: Design mode caps a design at three levels because a design has no diff, only a pull request does. A fourth narrative level also puts the runtime picture beside the file-changes slot the PR contract reserves, and touches more viewer call sites than the design needs.

alternatives.option: Upgrade the per-PR level-1 brief so PR diagrams follow the runtime contract
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer ruled it out: at PR stage the architecture is already written and the runtime diagram belongs to architecture:design. The per-PR contract stays diff-grounded, three levels.

alternatives.option: Enforce the review as a hard gate, three independent reviews all passing before design mode completes, as Nexus does with pass^3 before execution
alternatives.rejected_because: Nexus's gate evaluates executed work against a PRD; pre-code, our assessment discipline marks every finding kind prediction, and a numeric blocker would dress a prediction as a check. The reviewer enters stage 6 as advisory challenges first; the hard form stays available for implement Gate 2 if the advisory form proves toothless.

alternatives.option: Carry endpoints and data models as new fields inside intent.json
alternatives.rejected_because: intent.json is the interview record, and stage 2 deliberately collects five topics only. Endpoints and data models are drafted artifacts, not interview facts, so they belong in a separate contracts file the engineer shows before write, not in the author's stated intent.

out_of_scope: A DAG execution workflow or any orchestration engine; coding harnesses and models follow skill instructions, and RED/GREEN/VALIDATE already governs execution
The pass^k automated hard gate at design review; the stage-6 reviewer is advisory in this design
Any change to the per-PR diagram contract, its levels, or build_diagrams.py validation
Glossary Non-Goals work; intent.out_of_scope and goal.abort_if already cover them end to end
Ship a new agent file anywhere; the reviewer is session-spawned under the ADR-0005 dual-path pattern, and ADR-0025 keeps implement the only agent-owning plugin
risks: Mermaid's C4 rendering of clustered boundaries is weaker than Graphviz's dot clusters, so the 8-to-30-node rule may bind harder than Nexus did
The stage-6 reviewer adds spawn latency to every design round, and the churn-detection budget now shares room with reviewer retries
A blind rubric written from goal.json alone is thin pre-code, so scores can inflate; the mitigation is mandatory citation and the advisory classification
testing: uv run shared/build_index.py over the self bundle with the new design artifacts present; pytest on build_index and viewer tests; manual render of the design route in the View server; a real end-to-end run against the visualisation-decision-memory design in the think-with-ai repo, producing its runtime-architecture.mmd
reviewer_focus: The record-index shape: does record["diagrams"]["runtime"] break any of the viewer call sites that filter or read the diagrams dict
The blind rubric derivation: does the reviewer read goal.json and intent.json before the draft, and never the ADR
The contracts skip rule: a design with no public surface must state its skip, not go silent
unknowns: Whether mermaid C4 System_Boundary renders clusters acceptably across the viewer's themes
Whether one reviewer spawn per round is enough, or whether the round budget needs k configurable before E2 ships
